candidates.source_name: OPSI – Podatki o davčno potrjenih računih (FURS fiscal-verification open data)
candidates.why_relevant: Daily open dataset of the number and value of ALL fiscally verified invoices in Slovenia, broken to 5-digit SKD activity level. Because ZDavPR defines 'cash payment' broadly (banknotes/coins PLUS card and any non-direct-transfer settlement), this is the single largest merchant-side proxy for till-level transaction volume and value per retail sector — the denominator against which card/POS transaction counts can be benchmarked.
candidates.access_status: open, downloadable resources (CSV per year, e.g. DAVCNE_BLAGAJNE_2023)
candidates.legal_status: public sector open data, Slovenian open-data licence
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled scrape/API pull of the CKAN dataset page and its yearly resource files; parse DATE/SKD/NUMBER/AMOUNT; aggregate to retail SKD 47.x and hospitality 56.x
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on FURS open data terms
queries_used: podatki.gov.si FURS odprti podatki davčne blagajne računi zavezanci

candidates.source_name: FURS – Davčne blagajne in vezane knjige računov (fiscal verification programme pages)
candidates.why_relevant: The regulator's own programme area for davčno potrjevanje računov: legal definition of 'plačilo z gotovino' (which crucially includes card payments), obligations of merchants, supervision statistics and penalty reporting. Needed to correctly interpret any fiscal data and to understand what POS/ECR vendors must implement in Slovenia.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the Nadzor/Podrocja/Davcne_blagajne_in_VKR directory for PDF/DOCX; monitor for new 'Opis' and FAQ revisions
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball from open-data dataset publisher
queries_used: FURS davčno potrjevanje računov statistika način plačila gotovina

candidates.source_name: eDavki / FURS – Davčno potrjevanje računov: tehnične specifikacije
candidates.why_relevant: Technical spec (XML schemas, message fields, digital certificate rules) that every Slovenian ECR/POS software vendor must implement. Reveals exactly which fields — including payment-related ones — are transmitted per invoice, which bounds what fiscal data can ever show about card vs cash, and is a hard integration requirement for any POS/terminal vendor entering SI.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Version-diff monitoring of the spec index and linked XSD/PDF files
queries_used: FURS seznam proizvajalcev programske opreme davčne blagajne blagajniški programi Slovenija

candidates.source_name: Mercator Group – Annual reports / investor relations
candidates.why_relevant: Slovenia's largest grocery retailer by store count (~740 stores, ~30% share). Annual reports document store network size, checkout/self-checkout ('Tik-Tak' hitre blagajne) rollout, the Pika loyalty/payment card scheme and M Pay wallet — i.e. the acceptance footprint and own-scheme payment instruments of the biggest single POS estate in the country.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest from /assets/Annual-reports/ plus SEOnet cross-check; text-mine for 'blagajn', 'brezgotovinsk', 'Pika', 'samopostrežn'
queries_used: Mercator letno poročilo 2024 samopostrežne blagajne brezgotovinsko plačilo
Mercator Group letno poročilo za vlagatelje seonet.ljse.si

candidates.source_name: SEOnet (Ljubljanska borza) – issuer disclosures incl. Mercator
candidates.why_relevant: Regulated-information hub where Mercator and other listed SI issuers file annual/interim reports and corporate governance documents. Acts as a stable, machine-navigable pointer to retailer financials even when corporate sites reorganise; also surfaces bond prospectuses that describe the retail network in detail.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll issuer announcement feed filtered by issuer name; fetch AttachmentID PDFs
queries_used: Mercator Group letno poročilo za vlagatelje seonet.ljse.si Mercator maloprodajna mreža

candidates.source_name: Petrol Group – Annual report and investor disclosures
candidates.why_relevant: Petrol operates the densest unattended/attended retail payment network in SI (fuel stations, EV charging). Its reports cover the Petrol klub loyalty card and its successor 'Petrol Pay' payment card, plus retail transaction volumes — a rare case of a Slovenian merchant issuing its own payment instrument. Petrol has been publicly cited as roughly 50/50 cash vs card at the till.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual + semi-annual PDF harvest; also harvest Petrol klub / Petrol Pay terms-of-use PDFs which document card mechanics and acceptance network
queries_used: Petrol letno poročilo 2024 maloprodaja plačilna kartica Petrol klub

candidates.source_name: AJPES – JOLP public annual reports of retail companies (SPAR, Hofer, Lidl, Tuš, Jager)
candidates.why_relevant: Foreign-owned SI grocers (SPAR Slovenija ~EUR 1.16bn, Hofer ~EUR 674m, Lidl ~EUR 639m) are not listed and disclose only via AJPES statutory filings. This is the authoritative way to size the merchant-side transaction pool per chain and to track store-count and revenue growth that drives terminal and self-checkout demand.
candidates.access_status: public search (JOLP); some detail behind paid/registered services
candidates.legal_status: public register under Slovenian law; check reuse terms for bulk extraction
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted JOLP lookups by company registration number, annually after the March/April filing deadline; supplement with Bizi.si aggregation
queries_used: SPAR Slovenija Hofer Lidl Slovenija letno poročilo AJPES prihodki trgovine na drobno

candidates.source_name: Bizi.si – company financial profiles and retail-sector rankings
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of AJPES data that publishes ready-made 'largest Slovenian retailers' comparisons; far cheaper to monitor than filing-by-filing AJPES work, and its editorial pieces are a reliable annual pointer to who the top merchant counterparties are.
candidates.access_status: partly free, deeper data behind subscription
candidates.legal_status: commercial; scraping likely restricted by ToS — prefer manual/licensed use
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-volume retrieval of the annual retail-ranking articles; do not bulk-scrape
queries_used: SPAR Slovenija Hofer Lidl Slovenija letno poročilo AJPES prihodki trgovine na drobno
candidates.observed_blocker: Detailed financial screens require a subscription; headline articles are free

candidates.source_name: SURS / OPSI – Trgovina na drobno (retail trade turnover statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Official retail-trade turnover by broad merchandise group and by main activity — the macro denominator for merchant-side payments analysis. Combined with the FURS fiscal series it lets you separate 'total retail spend' from 'spend that passes through a fiscally verified till'.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PxWeb/SiStat API pull of TRG series; cache monthly releases
queries_used: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije trgovina statistika poročilo plačevanje gotovina kartice

candidates.source_name: GZS – Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije (Chamber of Commerce, trade section): current trade statistics
candidates.why_relevant: The merchants' own trade association: publishes curated current trade statistics, sector position papers and is the counterparty in policy debates on cash acceptance obligations and interchange/terminal costs. A prime pointer to merchant sentiment and to further merchant-side data.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of the trade-section pages and news; monitor for annual 'Trgovina' statistical briefings
queries_used: Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije trgovina statistika poročilo plačevanje gotovina kartice

candidates.source_name: Mikropis Holding / MikroPOS – Slovenian ECR and self-checkout vendor
candidates.why_relevant: The domestic incumbent in Slovenian retail checkout: installed the first self-checkouts in SI (Mercator 'Tik-Tak', 2007) and exports to China and South Korea (E-Mart). Its product and reference pages are the closest thing to a public inventory of self-checkout and ECR deployments in Slovenian retail — direct evidence of till-level automation and of the competitive landscape any POS/terminal vendor faces.
candidates.legal_status: public commercial content; vendor claims are self-reported
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl product/reference/news pages quarterly; cross-check deployment claims against retailer reports and trade press
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language vendor search + snowball into trade press
queries_used: Mikropis Špica blagajniški sistem trgovina reference Slovenija samopostrežne blagajne

candidates.source_name: Microgramm – davčne blagajne / SimPos ECR with integrated POS terminal
candidates.why_relevant: SME-segment fiscal cash register vendor bundling an ECR with a connected payment terminal (S1F2) at a published monthly rental price (~EUR 22.7 + VAT). Published pricing and bundle composition are hard evidence of the economics of merchant acceptance at the long tail of Slovenian retail and hospitality.
candidates.source_subtype: POS/ECR vendor site with public pricing
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly price/bundle snapshot of product pages for a terminal-cost time series
queries_used: blagajniški sistemi POS terminali Slovenija ponudniki reference trgovine

candidates.source_name: Krajnik d.o.o. – professional POS hardware distributor (Sunmi, Sam4s, EloPOS, Jassway, Shuttle)
candidates.why_relevant: Distributor catalogue revealing which POS hardware brands actually reach the Slovenian market and at what price points — an indirect but reliable read on terminal/ECR hardware supply chains and refresh cycles in SI retail and hospitality.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic catalogue snapshot; extract brand/model/price to track hardware mix
queries_used: blagajniški sistemi POS terminali Slovenija ponudniki reference trgovine

candidates.source_name: POS Elektronček – Slovenian POS/ECR and remote-ordering vendor
candidates.why_relevant: Established SI checkout vendor (GIS Order Android remote-ordering system) serving hospitality and retail; part of the domestic vendor map that determines how easily an acquirer or terminal vendor can integrate at the till.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual snapshot of product and reference pages
queries_used: blagajniški sistemi POS terminali Slovenija ponudniki reference trgovine

candidates.source_name: MetaKocka / Birokrat / Minimax / Vasco – cloud fiscal cash-register and ERP software vendors
candidates.why_relevant: Software layer of the Slovenian till: these vendors implement the FURS DPR interface and expose which accounting/POS ecosystems interoperate (Birokrat, Minimax, Pantheon, OpPIS, Vasco, Hermes). Their integration and export documentation maps the practical constraints on adding a card-acceptance flow to an SME merchant's checkout.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor vendor help-centre and blog feeds for DPR/payment-method changes
queries_used: FURS seznam proizvajalcev programske opreme davčne blagajne blagajniški programi Slovenija Birokrat Vasco Metakocka

candidates.source_name: Worldline / SIX Payment Services Slovenia – merchant acceptance product pages
candidates.why_relevant: Acquirer/PSP-side view of the SI merchant market: which schemes and wallets are accepted, terminal families offered (incl. Tap on Mobile softPOS), and how acceptance is packaged for small merchants. Directly documents what merchants can buy for card acceptance in Slovenia.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly snapshot of sl-SI merchant product and terminal pages; diff scheme/wallet lists
queries_used: Bankart Nexi Worldline Slovenija sprejemanje kartic trgovci POS terminal ponudba

candidates.source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – POS terminal management and servicing; annual reports
candidates.why_relevant: The Slovenian processor that operates and services a large share of the national POS estate for member banks and accepts international and local schemes (Maestro, MC, Visa, Amex, Diners, BA, Karanta, Activa). Its annual reports and service pages are the closest public description of who physically runs Slovenian merchant terminals.
candidates.source_subtype: card processor corporate site + annual report PDFs
candidates.access_status: open PDFs; older report URLs may have moved (unverified)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest from wp-content uploads; crawl 'ponudba' service pages
queries_used: Bankart Nexi Worldline Slovenija sprejemanje kartic trgovci POS terminal ponudba

candidates.source_name: 'Slovenija plačuje digitalno' (Visa + banks + GZS) programme pages
candidates.why_relevant: A named, dated market intervention explicitly targeting the weak spot of SI merchant acceptance: micro/small merchants. Publishes eligibility rules (free/subsidised terminal for at least 9 months for merchants with no card acceptance in the past 12 months) and participating banks (OTP, NLB). It is both a demand-side stimulus to track and an implicit admission of the size of the non-accepting merchant base.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Snapshot programme pages and partner-bank landing pages; watch for participation/uptake figures in press releases and ZBS commentary
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language programme search + snowball to partner banks and ZBS
queries_used: "Slovenija plačuje digitalno" Visa GZS trgovci brezgotovinsko sprejemanje kartic

candidates.source_name: Banka Slovenije – payment-instrument and POS/ATM statistics and cash strategy pages
candidates.why_relevant: Supplies the acceptance-side denominators quoted in merchant analysis: ~47,000 POS terminals at end-2024 (+11% y/y), 1,284 ATMs, contactless shares, and the SPACE-derived finding that nearly two thirds of physical-POS payments in SI were cash in 2024. Essential to normalise merchant-reported cash/card splits.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled pull of the payment-systems statistics tables and of publication/press-release feeds
queries_used: Banka Slovenije raziskava med trgovci sprejemanje gotovine plačilne kartice 2024 poročilo

candidates.source_name: Slovenian business/consumer press reporting merchant-level cash-vs-card splits (24ur, Žurnal24, Forbes SI, Siol, Svet kapitala)
candidates.why_relevant: Only public channel where individual Slovenian merchants disclose till-level payment mix — e.g. Petrol reporting roughly 50% of purchases in cash and Mercator somewhat under 60% cash. These merchant-sourced figures exist nowhere in official statistics and are the richest merchant-side quantitative signal available.
candidates.access_status: open; some outlets rate-limit or show consent walls
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted journalism — index and cite, do not republish
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword alerting on 'gotovina', 'plačilne kartice', 'blagajna', 'brezgotovinsko' plus retailer names; store links and extracted figures only, always trace back to the merchant as original claimant
queries_used: Banka Slovenije raziskava med trgovci sprejemanje gotovine plačilne kartice 2024 poročilo
Trgovinska zbornica Slovenije trgovina statistika poročilo plačevanje gotovina kartice

candidates.source_name: Retail technology trade press on SI self-checkout deployments (Retail Technology, iXtenso, ESM Magazine)
candidates.why_relevant: Documents named self-checkout deployments in Slovenia by international vendors (e.g. NCR self-checkouts ordered for 12 SPAR INTERSPAR hypermarkets) and supplies chain-level share and store-count context (Mercator ~742 stores / 30.5%; Spar ~134 stores / 26.7% in 2022). Complements the domestic vendor view with the international-vendor view of the same estate.
candidates.legal_status: copyrighted journalism — cite, do not republish
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword alerting on 'Slovenia' + self-checkout/POS/retail chain names; capture vendor-retailer pairings
queries_used: Slovenia retail merchants card acceptance POS terminals self-checkout Mercator Spar 2025

candidates.source_name: Commercial market-research reports on the Slovenia POS terminal market (Mordor Intelligence, Statista)
candidates.why_relevant: Vendor-side sizing and forecast of the SI POS terminal market (CAGR figures, segment splits) and long time series of terminal counts. Useful as a triangulation layer and for competitor/vendor share hypotheses, but methodology is opaque and headline numbers should never be preferred over Banka Slovenije counts.
candidates.legal_status: proprietary; licence required for reuse of figures
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Capture free summary metrics only; treat as hypothesis-generating, not authoritative
queries_used: Slovenia retail merchants card acceptance POS terminals self-checkout Mercator Spar 2025
candidates.observed_blocker: Full reports and most Statista series require paid subscription

candidates.source_name: Stripe – Payments in Slovenia market guide
candidates.why_relevant: PSP-authored country guide summarising merchant-relevant acceptance facts (card share of POS transaction value and count, contactless penetration, preferred local methods). Convenient orientation layer for the merchant acceptance mix, though derived from third-party data and commercially framed.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual snapshot; always trace cited figures back to their primary source
queries_used: Slovenia retail merchants card acceptance POS terminals self-checkout Mercator Spar 2025

negative_findings.description: The FURS fiscal-verification open dataset (DAVCNE_BLAGAJNE_*) exposes only DATE, SKD activity code, invoice COUNT and AMOUNT. Searches for a payment-instrument breakdown (gotovina vs kartica) inside the published fiscal data returned nothing.
negative_findings.result_summary: No public FURS series splitting fiscally verified invoices by tender type was located; the ZDavPR definition of 'plačilo z gotovino' deliberately lumps cash and card together, so the fiscal data structurally cannot separate them.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any attempt to derive cash-vs-card share at the Slovenian till from FURS data alone will be wrong. Card share must come from Banka Slovenije / acquirer data and be divided into the FURS totals, with the definitional mismatch documented.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for an official FURS register/list of certified fiscal cash-register software producers ('seznam proizvajalcev programske opreme za davčne blagajne').
negative_findings.result_summary: No authoritative public list surfaced across three query variations; only vendor self-declarations (Birokrat, MetaKocka, Minimax, Amstar) and interoperability lists on vendor sites were found. Slovenia appears not to operate a certification-and-publication regime for ECR software (unlike some neighbouring fiscalisation regimes).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There may be no single-source census of SI ECR/POS software vendors; the vendor map for this cell must be assembled bottom-up from vendor sites, distributor catalogues and integration lists, which is slower and incomplete.

negative_findings.description: Looked for retailer-published, structured statistics on cash vs card share at the till (Mercator, Spar, Hofer, Lidl, Petrol) in annual reports.
negative_findings.result_summary: No retailer was found to publish a payment-mix table. The only quantified merchant statements located are indirect press quotations (Petrol ~50% cash; Mercator somewhat under 60% cash).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Merchant-side payment mix in Slovenia is only obtainable via press quotes, direct enquiry, or association surveys — collection design must plan for qualitative extraction from news rather than structured reporting.

negative_findings.description: No public reference list of self-checkout or POS installations per Slovenian retail chain was found from either domestic (Mikropis/MikroPOS) or international vendors.
negative_findings.result_summary: Deployment evidence exists only as scattered press items (Mercator Tik-Tak since 2007; NCR self-checkouts for 12 SPAR INTERSPAR hypermarkets) rather than a maintained reference register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal/self-checkout estate size per chain must be estimated from store counts plus episodic press evidence, so any deployment figure carries wide uncertainty.

coverage_gaps.description: Discretionary and non-grocery merchant verticals were not covered in this pass: DIY/technical (Merkur, Bauhaus, Obi), drogerija (dm, Müller), fashion, and the hospitality/HoReCa till estate (SKD 56.x), which is a very large slice of fiscally verified invoices.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up sweep on SKD 47.x non-food and 56.x hospitality chains and their POS vendors; use the FURS open data's SKD dimension to prioritise verticals by invoice volume.

coverage_gaps.description: Acquirer-side merchant counts (number of merchant contracts, terminals per acquirer) for Slovenia were not located in public form; Bankart's role is described qualitatively but per-acquirer merchant/terminal splits were not found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check Banka Slovenije payment-statistics tables for acquirer-level breakdowns and mine bank annual reports (NLB, NKBM/OTP, SKB, Addiko, Sparkasse) for merchant-acquiring segment disclosures.

coverage_gaps.description: The FURS open-data resources sighted are per-year files; it is not established from this pass how far back the series runs, how quickly the current year is refreshed, or whether historic files are revised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate all resources on the CKAN dataset and record coverage start date, update cadence and revision behaviour before building any time-series product on it.

coverage_gaps.description: Italian- and Hungarian-language merchant sources for the bilingual border municipalities (Obalno-kraška, Prekmurje) were not searched, and no cross-border-shopping merchant angle was covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add it/hu query variants for merchant acceptance in bilingual areas if cross-border retail payment flows matter to the study.

coverage_gaps.description: The live Slovenian policy debate on mandatory cash acceptance and on obligatory card acceptance by merchants (referenced in Forbes SI reporting on Ministry of Finance proposals) was only touched at the edge; primary Ministry of Finance / draft-legislation sources were not pulled.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout gov.si (Ministrstvo za finance) and e-uprava public consultation portals for draft acts on payment acceptance obligations — a direct regulatory driver of merchant terminal demand.

brief: The Slovenian merchant/POS-side landscape has one unusually strong public asset: FURS fiscal-verification open data on podatki.gov.si, which reports the daily count and value of every fiscally verified invoice at 5-digit SKD level — but which, by legal design, folds card payments into 'cash payment' and therefore cannot itself yield a cash-vs-card split. Merchant-level payment mix is disclosed only anecdotally through the press (Petrol ~50% cash, Mercator somewhat under 60% cash), so the workable method is to combine FURS till volumes with Banka Slovenije acceptance statistics (~47,000 POS terminals at end-2024, +11% y/y) and with retailer disclosures via Mercator/SEOnet, Petrol IR and AJPES filings for the unlisted foreign-owned chains (Spar, Hofer, Lidl). The vendor layer is domestic and fragmented — Mikropis/MikroPOS (Mercator Tik-Tak self-checkouts, exports to Korea/China), Microgramm, POS Elektronček, Krajnik as hardware distributor, plus fiscal-software houses (Birokrat, MetaKocka, Minimax, Vasco) — with no official register of ECR software producers, so the vendor map must be built bottom-up. Acceptance economics at the long tail are being actively reshaped by the Visa/bank/GZS 'Slovenija plačuje digitalno' subsidised-terminal programme, which is both a tracked intervention and an admission of how thin card acceptance still is among micro and small SI merchants.
